intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Day Trip
experiences.description: Hop between the stunning Phi Phi Don and Phi Phi Leh islands by longtail boat, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters, exploring Maya Bay made famous by 'The Beach', and swimming in vibrant coral reefs teeming with tropical fish.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore the legendary street food scene of Yaowarat Road, Bangkok's Chinatown, sampling pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled skewers, boat noodles, and fresh seafood from bustling night market stalls while soaking in the vibrant atmosphere.

experiences.name: Similan Islands Snorkeling Adventure
experiences.description: Take a speedboat to the world-renowned Similan Islands National Park, one of Thailand's top diving and snorkeling destinations, featuring pristine white sand beaches, dramatic granite boulders, and some of the clearest waters in Southeast Asia.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Sunset Beach Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle a sea kayak along the serene mangrove-lined coastline of Koh Lanta, exploring hidden sea caves and secluded coves before arriving at Long Beach to watch a breathtaking Andaman Sea sunset with golden hues reflecting off calm waters.
experiences.location: Long Beach, Koh Lanta, Krabi Province

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Street Food & Night Bazaar Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the famous Sunday Walking Street and Night Bazaar in Chiang Mai's Old City, tasting northern Thai specialties like khao soi curry noodles, sai oua sausage, and crispy pork rinds while browsing handcrafted goods from local hill tribes.
experiences.location: Wualai Road & Night Bazaar, Old City, Chiang Mai

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, and take the Airport Rail Link or a budget taxi to your accommodation. Grab a quick late-night snack from a 7-Eleven or airport food stall. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and rest.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab snacks at the airport
meals.lunch: Skip or grab snacks at the airport
meals.dinner: 7-Eleven convenience store snacks or airport food court (budget ~150-200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Thai Baht ready for transport. A metered taxi from Suvarnabhumi to central Bangkok costs around 300-400 THB including expressway tolls. Download Google Maps offline and Grab app before landing.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. After a slow start, enjoy the hotel breakfast or head to a nearby local market for a traditional Thai breakfast. Explore the immediate beachfront area around Aegean Bliss Resort, take a morning stroll along the beach and get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area on foot or by renting a bicycle (~50-80 THB/hour). Visit a nearby temple or local market. If near Phuket or Koh Samui area, scope out local street food vendors and familiarize yourself with the neighborhood. Visit a local convenience store to stock up on essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest beach promenade or night market for dinner. Sample classic Thai street food dishes like Pad Thai, Som Tum, and Mango Sticky Rice. Watch the sunset from the beach and settle in for an early night to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Local Thai breakfast at a nearby market - Jok (rice porridge) or Khao Tom (150-200 THB)
meals.lunch: Street food stall near the hotel - Pad Kra Pao with rice and fried egg (~80-100 THB)
meals.dinner: Night market or beachside street food stalls - mixed dishes (~200-300 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at a local bank or SuperRich exchange booth for better rates. Avoid hotel currency exchange. October is the tail end of rainy season in some regions - carry a light rain poncho.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a local Buddhist temple (Wat) for a cultural experience. Many temples open at 6:00 AM. Watch monks during their morning alms-giving ceremony if available. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees). Return to the resort area for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the main beach area for snorkeling or swimming. Rent snorkeling gear from a local beach shack (~150-200 THB). Explore the shoreline and enjoy the crystal-clear waters. If near Phuket, visit Patong or Kata Beach. If near Koh Samui, explore Chaweng Beach area.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local night bazaar or walking street for dinner and souvenir shopping. Try grilled seafood skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut water. Browse handmade crafts and local goods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery - toast with eggs and coffee (~100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside food stall - grilled fish with rice or green papaya salad (~150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Night market street food spread - 3-4 dishes shared (~250-350 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect both your skin and the coral reefs. Bring a reusable water bottle to stay hydrated and reduce plastic waste.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island hopping tour. Book a budget group speedboat or longtail boat tour (500-800 THB per person) departing in the morning. Visit nearby smaller islands with stunning beaches and clear waters. Common stops include snorkeling spots, hidden lagoons, and sandbanks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping - enjoy swimming, snorkeling, and beach time at various island stops. Many budget tours include a simple lunch on the boat or at a beach restaurant on one of the islands.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon/early evening. Rest and freshen up, then head out for a casual beachside dinner. Enjoy the evening atmosphere with a cold Chang beer or fresh coconut.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the tour - grab a banana roti or toast from a street vendor (~60-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in tour package or simple beach restaurant on island (~150-200 THB if not included)
meals.dinner: Beachfront casual restaurant - Tom Yum soup, fried rice, and spring rolls (~250-350 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book island hopping tours through local guesthouses or directly at the pier to get the best budget rates. Avoid tourist agency markups. Bring waterproof bags for your electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter (~200-300 THB/day) or hire a songthaew (shared taxi) to explore the local area independently. Visit a viewpoint or hilltop for panoramic views of the coastline and surrounding islands. Take photos and enjoy the scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local fishing village to experience authentic Thai coastal life. Chat with fishermen, browse a local fresh market, and try freshly caught seafood. Visit a less-touristy beach for a quieter experience away from the crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or watch a street food vendor prepare fresh pad thai at a roadside stall. Enjoy dinner at a local Thai restaurant frequented by locals rather than tourists for authentic flavors and lower prices. Try Massaman curry or Panang curry.

meals.breakfast: Local market - Khao Niao Mamuang (mango sticky rice) or fresh fruit (~80-120 THB)
meals.lunch: Fishing village seafood - grilled squid or shrimp with rice (~150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant - curry with rice, soup, and a drink (~200-280 THB)

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter, always wear a helmet and carry your passport or a copy. Check if your travel insurance covers scooter accidents. Drive on the left side of the road in Thailand.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby national park or nature reserve. Many coastal areas in Thailand have jungle-covered hills with hiking trails and waterfalls. Pack water and snacks for the hike. Enjoy the lush tropical scenery and wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a waterfall within the national park for a refreshing swim in natural pools. Spend time relaxing in nature before heading back to the resort area. Stop at a roadside fruit stand for fresh tropical fruits like rambutan, mangosteen, or durian.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a relaxing evening. Head to a local beach bar for a sundowner drink (cheap local beer ~60-80 THB). Have dinner at a street food cluster and try new dishes you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or guesthouse breakfast - eggs, toast, and coffee (~100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or national park food stall - fried rice or noodles (~100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food cluster - Pad See Ew, spring rolls, and Thai iced tea (~200-280 THB)

day_by_day.notes: National park entrance fees are typically 200-300 THB for foreigners. Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes for hiking. Bring insect repellent for jungle areas.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy beach morning - wake up naturally and enjoy the resort's beachfront. Go for a morning swim, practice yoga on the beach, or simply relax with a book. This is a rest day mid-trip to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat to a nearby secluded beach or snorkeling spot that's harder to reach by land (~200-400 THB for a private longtail). Spend a few hours swimming, sunbathing, and exploring tide pools. Bring your own snacks and drinks to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer sit-down dinner at a mid-range local restaurant (still budget-friendly). Try a seafood feast - grilled prawns, steamed fish with lime and chili, and papaya salad. This is your weekly treat meal.

meals.breakfast: Slow morning - fresh fruit smoothie and banana pancake from a beach vendor (~100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack your own snacks or eat at a simple beach shack (~100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Mid-range local seafood restaurant - full meal with drinks (~400-500 THB as a treat)

day_by_day.notes: Halfway through the trip! Review your budget spending so far and adjust for the remaining days. Check if you need to book any upcoming transport or tours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local cooking class or food market tour in the morning (budget cooking classes: 500-800 THB). Learn to make 3-4 classic Thai dishes like Tom Kha Gai, Pad Thai, and Green Curry. This is both a cultural experience and a practical skill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local craft market or artisan village in the afternoon. Browse handmade goods, local textiles, and unique souvenirs. Practice bargaining respectfully - start at 50-60% of the asking price. Visit a local pharmacy for any travel necessities.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the dishes you cooked in the morning class for dinner, or head to a street food area. Visit a local bar for live music or cultural performance if available. Try a Thai cocktail made with local spirits.

meals.breakfast: Pre-cooking class breakfast - congee or noodle soup from a street vendor (~80-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Food cooked during the cooking class (usually included in the class fee)
meals.dinner: Street food or leftovers from cooking class (~150-250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes are a great budget-friendly activity that provides both entertainment and a meal. Many classes include a market tour as part of the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Second island hopping adventure to different islands than Day 4. Book a different route to discover new spots. Look for tours that visit less-visited islands for a more authentic experience. Depart early morning to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy extended time at the most beautiful island stop. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax on pristine beaches. Many longtail boat captains can be hired privately for a half-day at around 1,000-1,500 THB for the whole boat (split among group members).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk followed by dinner at a beachside restaurant. Try Khao Pad (fried rice) with seafood or Pla Kapong Neung Manao (steamed sea bass with lime). End the evening with a Thai massage (~300-400 THB for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure - roti with condensed milk and coffee (~80-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Island beach restaurant or tour-included lunch (~150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant - seafood fried rice and soup (~250-350 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Thai massage is extremely affordable and a must-try experience. Look for licensed massage shops slightly away from tourist areas for better prices and quality.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local temple complex for a deeper cultural experience. Spend time observing monks, exploring temple grounds, and learning about Thai Buddhism. Many temples have monks who speak English and welcome respectful conversation with tourists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local fresh market (Talad) in the afternoon when vendors are active. Sample exotic fruits, local snacks, and fresh juices. Buy some Thai snacks and treats to take home as edible souvenirs. Visit a local pharmacy or traditional herbal shop.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the most popular street food area or night market for a big street food crawl dinner. Try as many different dishes as possible - Satay skewers, Pad Thai, Moo Ping (grilled pork skewers), Khao Man Gai, and Thai desserts.

meals.breakfast: Temple area food stall - sticky rice with grilled chicken (~80-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Fresh market snacks and fruit - sampling various items (~150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Night market street food crawl - multiple dishes (~300-400 THB)

day_by_day.notes: When visiting temples, always remove shoes before entering the main hall, dress modestly, and speak quietly. Never point your feet toward Buddha images or monks.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking or paddleboarding session (rent equipment for 200-300 THB/hour). Explore the coastline, sea caves, or mangrove forests by kayak. This is one of the most beautiful ways to experience Thailand's coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a beach that you haven't explored yet. Spend the afternoon relaxing, swimming, and soaking in the last full beach days of the trip. Collect any last-minute souvenirs from beach vendors. Try fresh coconut ice cream (~50 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner preparation - visit a local supermarket and buy ingredients for a picnic or beach dinner. Alternatively, splurge on a final seafood dinner at a recommended local restaurant. Reflect on the trip highlights over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-kayaking light breakfast - banana and yogurt or toast (~80-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Beach shack or food cart near the kayaking area (~150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Special local seafood restaurant or beach picnic (~350-450 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing non-essential items tonight. Check airline baggage allowances and consider shipping home any extra items if you've bought too many souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the beach - take one last swim and enjoy the resort's beachfront. Pack up your belongings and check out of the resort (or arrange late checkout if available). Store luggage at the hotel while you enjoy your last day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final exploration of the local area. Visit any spots you may have missed. Buy last-minute souvenirs, Thai snacks, and gifts for people back home. Stop at a local pharmacy for Tiger Balm, herbal products, or other Thai specialties to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Final street food dinner in Thailand - make it memorable by revisiting your favorite food stall or dish from the trip. Enjoy a final Thai iced tea or Chang beer while watching the local evening life. Begin making your way to your departure point.

meals.breakfast: Last Thai breakfast - Jok (rice porridge) with century egg and ginger (~100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Favorite street food dish from the trip as a farewell meal (~150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Final street food spread at the night market (~250-350 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Thai Baht for last-minute expenses, transport to the airport, and airport meals. Most airports have currency exchange booths but rates are poor - spend remaining Baht on food and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand. If time permits before departure, enjoy a last walk along the beach or a final Thai breakfast. Begin making your way to the airport well in advance - aim to arrive at least 3 hours before international flights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport departure procedures - check in, clear immigration, and browse duty-free shops. Pick up any last-minute Thai souvenirs at the airport (Doi Kham products, Thai silk items, or packaged Thai snacks). Enjoy a final Thai meal at the airport food court.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Thailand filled with stunning beaches, island adventures, and unforgettable street food experiences. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Hotel or guesthouse area - final Thai breakfast or convenience store items (~100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport food court - Pad Thai or rice dish (~200-300 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: A well-planned budget trip to Thailand for 13 days can be done for approximately 1,500-2,500 THB per day (~$40-70 USD) including accommodation, food, transport, and activities. Always keep emergency funds accessible. Take photos of all important documents before leaving Thailand.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange private transfer or airport taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in transit
meals.lunch: N/A - in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the resort or grab a quick bite from a nearby 7-Eleven or late-night street food stall near the resort entrance

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-arrange airport transfer with your resort to avoid hassle after a long flight. Exchange some currency at the airport for initial expenses. October is late rainy season in Thailand - occasional showers possible but generally manageable.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront to orient yourself with the surroundings and soak in your first full Thai morning. Explore the resort facilities and nearby beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local market or beach town center for a gentle orientation stroll. Visit any nearby temples or viewpoints within easy reach of the resort. Rent a beach chair and relax by the sea, dipping your toes in the warm Gulf of Thailand or Andaman waters.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest beach road or night market for your first real taste of Thai street food. Try pad thai from a street vendor, fresh grilled seafood skewers, and mango sticky rice for dessert. Enjoy a casual beachside dinner as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a nearby local café serving Thai-style breakfast with rice porridge (jok) and fried eggs
meals.lunch: Light meal at a beachside restaurant - try a classic green curry or som tum (papaya salad) for around 150-250 THB
meals.dinner: Night market street food - pad thai, grilled satay skewers, fresh coconut, and mango sticky rice (budget 200-350 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Keep the pace relaxed today to recover from jet lag. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen generously. October weather may include afternoon rain showers - carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise beach walk before the heat kicks in. Join a local longtail boat tour departing from the nearest pier for a half-day island hopping excursion to nearby smaller islands or snorkeling spots. Explore crystal-clear waters and coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the morning boat tour and have lunch at a beachside shack. Spend the afternoon exploring sea caves, hidden lagoons, or simply snorkeling off the main beach. Rent snorkel gear from a local shop (around 150-200 THB) if not included in the tour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up. Head out for dinner at a mid-range Thai restaurant near the beach. Try massaman curry, tom yum soup, and grilled fish. Afterward, enjoy a relaxed beachside drink at a bar with live acoustic music.

meals.breakfast: Thai-style breakfast at a local café - rice soup with pork, Thai iced tea, and fresh tropical fruit (100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant - grilled prawns, steamed rice, and papaya salad (300-450 THB)
meals.dinner: Mid-range Thai restaurant dinner - massaman curry, tom yum, steamed jasmine rice, and a local Singha beer (400-600 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the island hopping boat tour the evening before through your resort or a local tour operator. Group tours cost around 800-1,500 THB per person and typically include snorkeling equipment and a light lunch.

day_by_day.morning: Take a cooking class at a local Thai cooking school near the resort area. Learn to make 3-4 classic Thai dishes including tom kha gai, pad kra pao, and mango sticky rice. Classes typically run 3-4 hours and include a market visit to source fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class, visit the local fresh market to browse exotic fruits, spices, and street snacks. Pick up fresh coconut water, rambutan, and dragon fruit to snack on. Explore any nearby cultural sites such as a local Buddhist temple (wat) - dress respectfully with covered shoulders and knees.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset kayaking session along the coastline, paddling through mangroves or sea caves if available nearby. Return to the resort and dine at the resort restaurant or a nearby beachfront venue. Try a seafood platter and fresh-caught fish of the day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast included as part of the cooking class market visit, or grab fresh fruit and pastries from a local bakery (80-120 THB)
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared in the cooking class - most cooking schools serve your creations as the midday meal
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant with fresh seafood - whole grilled fish, stir-fried vegetables, and coconut ice cream for dessert (500-700 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically cost 1,200-1,800 THB per person and are one of the best value experiences in Thailand. Book in advance as popular classes fill up quickly. Kayak rentals are approximately 200-400 THB per hour.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a full-day island hopping adventure to more distant islands. Depart early by speedboat or traditional ferry to explore multiple islands in the area - visit white sand beaches, hidden coves, and vibrant coral reefs. Snorkel among tropical fish and colorful sea life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island hopping tour with a stop at a less-visited island for a private beach picnic lunch. Explore the jungle interior of a larger island via a short hiking trail. Look for monitor lizards, tropical birds, and exotic flora along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon. Shower and rest at the resort. Head out for a street food dinner at a local night bazaar - try khao man gai (poached chicken rice), boat noodles, and grilled corn. End the evening with a traditional Thai herbal tea.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure - toast, eggs, and fresh juice (included or 150-200 THB)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch provided by the tour operator on a remote island beach, or buy fresh seafood grilled on the spot at an island beach shack (300-400 THB)
meals.dinner: Night bazaar street food crawl - try 4-5 different dishes from various stalls (200-350 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Full-day speedboat island hopping tours cost approximately 1,500-2,500 THB per person. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag for valuables, and motion sickness tablets if needed. Seas in October can be slightly choppy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a rest morning at the resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast and spend time by the pool or beach. Practice yoga on the beach at sunrise if available through the resort or a nearby studio. Read, relax, and recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or hire a local tuk-tuk to explore the surrounding area independently. Visit viewpoints, hidden beaches, fishing villages, and local temples not covered on group tours. Stop at roadside stalls for fresh coconut water and tropical snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage at a reputable local spa (1-hour Thai massage costs approximately 300-500 THB). Afterward, enjoy a romantic or relaxed dinner at a slightly upscale beachfront restaurant with candles and sea views.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed resort breakfast or a nearby café with smoothie bowls, fresh fruit platters, and Thai iced coffee (200-300 THB)
meals.lunch: Local village eatery or roadside restaurant during the scooter exploration - try khao pad (fried rice) or noodle soup (80-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Mid-range beachfront restaurant - seafood pasta or Thai-fusion dishes, fresh fish, and a glass of house wine (600-900 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental costs approximately 250-400 THB per day. Always wear a helmet, carry your international driving permit, and drive cautiously on local roads. Negotiate tuk-tuk fares before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Join an early morning fishing trip with local fishermen departing before dawn. Experience traditional Thai fishing techniques, help cast nets, and enjoy the serene beauty of the sea at sunrise. A truly authentic and memorable cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return with the catch of the morning. Visit a nearby floating market or fresh seafood market to see the day's haul being sold. Have a long, leisurely lunch at a waterfront restaurant. Spend the rest of the afternoon at the beach swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Thai cultural show if available in the area, featuring classical dance, Muay Thai demonstrations, and traditional music. Alternatively, join a beachside fire show at one of the beach bars. Enjoy cocktails and the lively beach atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light snacks and coffee provided on the fishing boat, or eat before departure at the resort (100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Waterfront seafood restaurant featuring fresh catch - grilled whole fish, tom yum seafood soup, and steamed rice (400-600 THB)
meals.dinner: Beach bar dinner with casual Thai food - fish and chips Thai-style, spring rolls, and tropical cocktails (400-600 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fishing trips can be arranged through local tour operators or directly with fishermen at the pier. Cost is approximately 800-1,200 THB per person for a half-day trip. This is the midpoint of your trip - a great time to do laundry at the resort laundry service.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and travel to a new destination island or beach town to continue your island hopping adventure. Take a ferry or speedboat to your next location. Arrive, check in to a new mid-range guesthouse or beach bungalow, and explore the new area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the new destination on foot. Walk along the main beach, browse local shops for souvenirs and beach gear, and discover the unique character of this new location. Visit a local viewpoint for panoramic photos of the surrounding islands and sea.
day_by_day.evening: Discover the new area's street food scene. Visit the local night market and try regional specialties unique to this part of Thailand. Chat with local vendors and fellow travelers to get insider tips on the best spots in the area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before checkout or grab something at the ferry pier (150-200 THB)
meals.lunch: Quick meal at the pier or on the ferry - pre-packed Thai food or a snack from a pier-side vendor (100-200 THB)
meals.dinner: New destination night market - explore new flavors and regional dishes (200-350 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets between major Thai islands cost approximately 200-600 THB depending on distance. Book in advance during peak season. Mid-range beach bungalows at the new destination should cost 800-1,500 THB per night.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the new island's most famous beach or natural attraction in the morning before crowds arrive. Hike to a jungle waterfall if available, or kayak through sea caves and hidden lagoons. Hire a local guide for more in-depth exploration (500-800 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a snorkeling or diving excursion from the new island's pier. The new location may offer different marine life and reef ecosystems compared to your previous base. Try a beginner scuba dive with a certified instructor if you haven't dived before.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beachside barbecue dinner at one of the island's popular evening spots. Fresh seafood grilled over charcoal, including lobster, tiger prawns, squid, and fish - choose your catch and have it cooked to order. Watch the stars over the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Local guesthouse breakfast or a nearby café - fresh baguette with jam (Thai-French influence), tropical fruit, and coffee (150-200 THB)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach shack after snorkeling - fried rice, spring rolls, and fresh coconut (200-300 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachside BBQ seafood dinner - choose fresh seafood by weight and have it grilled (600-1,000 THB per person depending on selection)

day_by_day.notes: Beginner scuba diving (Discover Scuba) costs approximately 2,500-3,500 THB and includes equipment, instructor, and 1-2 dives. No certification required. PADI Open Water courses are also available if you want to get certified (10,000-15,000 THB for the full course).

day_by_day.morning: Take a long-tail boat to one of the more remote and less-visited beaches or islands in the area for a half-day private escape. Bring snacks, drinks, and snorkeling gear. Enjoy a secluded beach almost entirely to yourself - swim, explore tide pools, and collect shells.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the main island and spend the afternoon exploring the inland areas. Visit a rubber plantation or coconut farm for a unique agricultural experience. Learn about Thailand's important role in global rubber production. Sample fresh coconut products.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a street food tour with a local guide who takes you to the best hidden gems of the local food scene. Try dishes you might not have discovered on your own, including regional curries, fermented fish dishes, and unique local desserts.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the boat trip - Thai-style omelette on rice with chili sauce and fresh orange juice (100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the secluded beach with pre-packed food from a local market - fresh fruit, sandwiches, and snacks (150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food tour dinner with a local guide - approximately 600-900 THB per person including guide fee and all food tastings

day_by_day.notes: Private long-tail boat hire for a half-day costs approximately 1,000-1,500 THB. Negotiate directly at the pier in the morning. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen for the secluded beach visit as there may be no facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the local temple complex for a morning meditation session or simply to experience the peaceful atmosphere of Thai Buddhist culture. Participate in the early morning monk alms-giving ceremony (tak bat) if available - a deeply spiritual and culturally significant experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a beach club or water sports center. Try stand-up paddleboarding, windsurfing, or parasailing for an adrenaline rush over the turquoise waters. Alternatively, relax at a beach club with a pool, music, and refreshing drinks.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local pier area at sunset for stunning golden hour photography. Dine at a highly-rated local restaurant recommended by guesthouse staff. Order a chef's tasting selection of Thai dishes to experience a variety of flavors in one sitting.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the temple visit - fresh fruit smoothie and toast from a local café (100-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch - burgers, salads, and fresh juices in a relaxed setting (350-500 THB)
meals.dinner: Recommended local restaurant - chef's selection of 5-6 Thai dishes shared family-style with steamed rice (500-700 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: When visiting temples, always dress modestly - cover shoulders and knees. Sarongs are often available to borrow at temple entrances. Remove shoes before entering temple buildings. Water sports rentals cost approximately 300-800 THB per activity.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to souvenir shopping at local markets and craft shops. Look for handmade items including silk scarves, hand-painted ceramics, carved wooden figurines, and locally made jewelry. Practice your bargaining skills at the market - start at 50-60% of the asking price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy one final island hopping excursion or a sunset cruise around the local islands. Many operators offer 3-4 hour afternoon sunset cruises with drinks and snacks included, visiting sea caves and hidden beaches as the light turns golden.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your final full evening in Thailand with a special dinner at the best restaurant in the area. Splurge slightly on a seafood feast or a Thai fine-dining experience. Toast to an incredible trip with a cocktail featuring local Thai rum or a classic Thai iced tea.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort or guesthouse breakfast - full spread with eggs, toast, tropical fruit, and coffee (200-300 THB)
meals.lunch: Quick and casual lunch between shopping - try a local noodle shop for a bowl of boat noodles or pad see ew (80-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a top-rated local restaurant - splurge on a seafood platter, premium curries, and a dessert platter (800-1,200 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Set a souvenir budget before shopping to avoid overspending. Good value souvenirs include Thai silk products, spice sets, coconut oil products, and handmade elephant figurines. Sunset cruises cost approximately 800-1,500 THB per person with drinks included.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a final morning swim in the warm Thai waters. Pack your bags and check out of the accommodation. Store luggage with the guesthouse if your departure is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend any remaining time exploring a final local attraction or simply relaxing at a café with a Thai iced coffee. Visit a local pharmacy to stock up on affordable Thai health products like tiger balm, herbal muscle rubs, and vitamin supplements to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Make your way to the airport or ferry pier for your onward journey. Grab a final Thai street food meal at the airport or departure terminal. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, island hopping, and unforgettable street food experiences across Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast - khao tom (rice porridge) with ginger and century egg, or a full café breakfast (150-200 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport or pier food court - pad thai, green curry, or a quick noodle soup (150-250 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or departure lounge meal - treat yourself to one last Thai dish before flying (300-500 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2-3 hours before international flights and 1.5 hours before domestic flights. Declare any food items or large purchases at customs. Keep some Thai Baht for airport transport and last-minute purchases. Many Thai airports have excellent duty-free shopping.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in with welcome amenities including chilled towels, tropical fruit platter, and a complimentary welcome cocktail. Brief orientation with personal concierge to plan the journey ahead. Settle into your beachfront suite and enjoy the sound of the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining from the resort's premium menu — recommended: Tom Kha Gai soup, jasmine rice with grilled sea bass, and a selection of Thai desserts delivered to your suite

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Request early check-in amenities and a pillow menu. Keep the first night light — rest is the priority after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. Indulge in a beachfront breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant. Take a gentle morning stroll along the private beach to acclimate to the tropical surroundings. Arrange a 90-minute traditional Thai herbal compress massage at the resort spa to recover from jet lag.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate coastal area with a guided resort-arranged snorkeling excursion in the crystal-clear waters just off the beachfront. Discover vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish. Return to the resort for a refreshing dip in the infinity pool overlooking the Andaman Sea or Gulf of Thailand. Enjoy a tropical fruit smoothie from the pool bar.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's overwater bar — try a classic Thai Basil Smash or a Lychee Martini. Dinner at the resort's fine-dining beachfront restaurant featuring a curated Thai tasting menu with wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront restaurant — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, tropical fruit platter, freshly brewed Thai coffee and fresh coconut water
meals.lunch: Pool-side light bites — grilled tiger prawns with nam jim sauce, papaya salad, and chilled coconut sorbet
meals.dinner: Resort fine-dining — 7-course Thai tasting menu featuring Massaman lamb, steamed blue crab with glass noodles, and mango sticky rice with coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: October in Thailand can bring occasional afternoon showers — keep a light rain jacket handy. The spa should be booked in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a private sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged by the resort. Follow with a nourishing breakfast. Head out on a private longtail boat tour to explore hidden sea caves, limestone karsts, and secluded lagoons in the surrounding bay area — a quintessential Thai coastal experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby floating village or stilted fishing community for an authentic cultural encounter. Enjoy a private cooking class on board or at a local venue — learn to prepare Pad Thai, Green Curry, and Som Tum from a professional Thai chef using fresh market ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset swim. Dine at a highly-rated local seafood restaurant near the resort, known for its fresh catch grilled over charcoal and served with traditional Thai condiments.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant — congee with century egg and pork, dim sum basket, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Freshly prepared dishes from the cooking class — enjoy what you cook in a scenic setting
meals.dinner: Premium local seafood restaurant — whole grilled barramundi with garlic and chili, oysters with lime dressing, and coconut-based seafood curry

day_by_day.notes: The private longtail boat tour should be arranged through the concierge the day before. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and water shoes for the boat excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Depart after an early breakfast for a full-day island hopping excursion via private speedboat. First stop: a pristine uninhabited island with powdery white sand and turquoise water — perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Explore the underwater world with premium snorkeling gear provided on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a second island known for its dramatic viewpoints and jungle interior. Hike to a panoramic overlook with a knowledgeable local guide. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort and packed in a premium hamper, served on the beach under the shade of palm trees.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a private in-villa dinner on your terrace — candles, flowers, and a personalized menu curated by the resort's executive chef. Toast the evening with a bottle of chilled champagne.

meals.breakfast: Resort — avocado toast with poached eggs, smoked salmon, tropical fruit bowl, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet beach picnic hamper — artisan sandwiches, cold cuts, cheese, Thai rice salad, fresh fruit, sparkling water, and rosé wine
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dining — pan-seared lobster tail, truffle jasmine rice, sautéed morning glory, and a decadent chocolate lava cake

day_by_day.notes: Private speedboat island hopping must be booked 48 hours in advance. Bring waterproof bags for electronics. Apply waterproof sunscreen liberally throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow morning at the resort. Take advantage of the resort's water sports facilities — try stand-up paddleboarding or sea kayaking along the coastline. Alternatively, book a second spa treatment — a traditional Thai oil massage or a Hammam-style body scrub and wrap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private transfer to the nearest town or market area for a premium street food tour with a local food guide. Sample iconic Thai street food: Pad Kra Pao (basil stir-fry), Hoi Tod (crispy oyster omelette), Kanom Krok (coconut pancakes), and fresh-cut tropical fruits. Visit a local wet market to observe the vibrant food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the town's night market — browse artisan crafts, handmade jewelry, and local textiles. Enjoy a casual but high-quality dinner at a beloved local restaurant favored by discerning travelers, known for its authentic regional Thai cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort — full Thai breakfast spread: rice porridge, fried eggs, Thai sausage, pickled vegetables, and jasmine tea
meals.lunch: Premium street food tour — curated tastings across 6–8 street food stalls with your private guide
meals.dinner: Acclaimed local restaurant — Southern Thai curry with crab, stir-fried pork with holy basil, and sticky rice with durian custard

day_by_day.notes: Carry small Thai baht notes for street food stalls. The food guide should be a licensed local expert — arrange through the concierge. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market tour.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for a full-day trip to a celebrated nearby island or national marine park. Board a private catamaran for a luxury sailing experience. Anchor at a world-famous snorkeling spot and dive into the clear waters teeming with marine life including sea turtles and colorful reef fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sail to a secluded beach for a relaxed afternoon. Enjoy freshly prepared Thai food and cold drinks served on the catamaran by the onboard crew. Swim, sunbathe, and explore rock pools. Optional: try scuba diving with a certified instructor for an introductory dive in the warm tropical waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sail back as the sun sets over the horizon — a magical golden hour on the open water. Return to the resort and unwind with a soak in your private plunge pool or bathtub. Dinner at the resort's second restaurant specializing in contemporary Asian fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort — smoothie bowls, granola, Greek yogurt, fresh mango, and espresso
meals.lunch: Onboard catamaran catering — grilled seafood skewers, Thai green mango salad, coconut rice, cold beers and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Resort Asian fusion restaurant — wagyu beef tataki with ponzu, miso-glazed Chilean sea bass, and yuzu panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Confirm catamaran availability and crew size with concierge. Scuba diving requires a basic health declaration form. Bring a light layer for the breezy evening sail back.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint rest day — embrace the resort lifestyle. Begin with a guided meditation session on the beach at sunrise. Enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning reading, swimming, or simply relaxing in a private beachfront cabana with personalized butler service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a Thai fruit carving or flower garland (Phuang Malai) workshop hosted at the resort — a beautiful cultural craft experience. Alternatively, visit the resort's boutique for curated Thai artisan goods and premium souvenirs. Enjoy afternoon tea with Thai-inspired pastries and herbal teas.
day_by_day.evening: Dress up for a special evening — arrange a private beachside dinner set up by the resort team with torches, flowers, and a personalized menu. Watch the stars emerge over the ocean as you dine in complete privacy and luxury.

meals.breakfast: Resort — eggs your way, freshly baked croissants, charcuterie board, tropical juices, and barista-crafted coffee
meals.lunch: Resort afternoon tea — finger sandwiches, scones with clotted cream, Thai-spiced macarons, pandan cake, and premium loose-leaf teas
meals.dinner: Private beachside dinner — chilled seafood tower, grilled whole lobster with herb butter, saffron rice, and a bespoke dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: The private beachside dinner setup requires 24 hours' notice and may carry an additional setup fee — confirm with the resort's butler team. This is an ideal evening for a special occasion celebration.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort after a final breakfast. Private luxury transfer to the pier or airport for onward travel to a second Thai island destination (e.g., Koh Lanta, Koh Phi Phi, Koh Yao Noi, or Koh Tao depending on resort location). Arrive and check into a second luxury property — a clifftop villa or overwater bungalow for a change of scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the new accommodation and explore the immediate surroundings on foot or by bicycle. Visit a nearby viewpoint for panoramic island vistas. Take a refreshing dip in the new property's pool or the beach directly below.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the island's most celebrated beach bar or sunset viewpoint to watch the legendary Thai sunset. Enjoy cocktails and canapés as the sky turns shades of amber and pink. Dinner at a renowned beachside restaurant on the new island.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — final farewell breakfast with a la carte selections and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light meal during transit — premium airport lounge or ferry snacks, or a quick stop at a well-regarded local café upon arrival
meals.dinner: Island restaurant — freshly caught grilled fish of the day, spicy seafood noodle soup, and coconut pudding with palm sugar

day_by_day.notes: Confirm ferry schedules or domestic flight times well in advance. Arrange luggage handling and transfer logistics with the concierge the evening before. October weather may affect ferry services — have a backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Rise at dawn for a magical sunrise kayaking tour through mangrove forests and sea caves with a private guide. The early morning light through the mangroves is extraordinary. Return to the hotel for a hearty breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a premium full-day island hopping tour visiting 3–4 smaller surrounding islands. Highlights include a hidden emerald lagoon accessible only by kayak at low tide, a white sand sandbar that appears at low tide, and a coral garden for snorkeling. Gourmet lunch is served on the boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the accommodation and enjoy a sunset couples or solo massage at the hotel spa using traditional Thai techniques with aromatic lemongrass and kaffir lime oils. Dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel restaurant — chia pudding, fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and cold brew Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Onboard boat lunch — Thai fried rice with prawns, larb salad, grilled corn, and fresh watermelon
meals.dinner: Hotel signature restaurant — Southern Thai Massaman duck curry, jasmine rice, stir-fried water spinach, and sticky mango rice

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking through mangroves is tide-dependent — confirm the best timing with your guide. Bring a dry bag and waterproof phone case. The sandbar visit is also tide-dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning to relax at the hotel or explore the local village on foot. Visit a local fresh market in the morning to observe daily island life — vendors selling fresh fish, tropical produce, and local snacks. Pick up some fresh fruit for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private longtail boat to take you to a secluded beach only accessible by water — bring a book, snorkeling gear, and a picnic. Spend the afternoon in complete solitude on your own private slice of paradise. The boat captain waits nearby and returns you at your chosen time.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the island's street food scene after dark — visit the local night market for an authentic culinary adventure. Try Satay with peanut sauce, Roti with condensed milk, Moo Ping (grilled pork skewers), and fresh coconut ice cream served in a coconut shell.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — full Thai breakfast with rice soup, fried egg, Thai sausages, fresh fruit, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Picnic on the secluded beach — prepared by the hotel: sandwiches, Thai cold noodle salad, tropical fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Local night market street food tour — budget approximately 300–500 THB per person for a diverse spread of authentic local dishes

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate the longtail boat hire through the hotel concierge for the best rate and a trusted captain. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a beach umbrella for the secluded beach afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning cooking class at a local culinary school or with a private chef — focus on Northern or Southern Thai cuisine depending on the island. Learn to make Tom Yum from scratch, craft a perfect Pad Thai, and prepare a traditional Thai dessert. The class includes a market visit to source fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the island's most important Buddhist temple or cultural landmark. Dress respectfully (shoulders and knees covered) and take time to observe monks, admire intricate architecture, and make a small offering. Explore any nearby artisan workshops or craft villages.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the penultimate night with a premium dining experience — book a table at the island's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurant, ideally one with a clifftop or overwater setting. Opt for a chef's tasting menu with wine or cocktail pairings.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — fresh baked goods, yogurt parfait, tropical fruit platter, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class — a full Thai meal you prepared yourself, served in a beautiful setting
meals.dinner: Island's premier fine-dining restaurant — chef's 8-course tasting menu featuring local seafood, foraged herbs, and artisan desserts with paired wines

day_by_day.notes: Temple visits require modest dress — the hotel can provide sarongs if needed. Fine-dining reservations must be made at least 48 hours in advance. This is one of the culinary highlights of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — make the most of it with an early morning stand-up paddleboard session at sunrise, gliding across glassy calm water as the island wakes up. Follow with a long, leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Visit the hotel spa for a final indulgent treatment — a full-body scrub and wrap with tropical ingredients like turmeric, coconut milk, and pandan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last beach afternoon — claim a prime spot on the resort's beachfront, order cocktails from the beach butler, and soak in the stunning scenery. Take a final swim in the warm Andaman or Gulf waters. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — look for hand-painted silk scarves, premium Thai tea blends, artisan ceramics, and locally made coconut products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — return to your favorite restaurant from the trip or try one last new venue. Toast the incredible journey with a bottle of fine wine or a signature Thai cocktail. Reflect on the memories made over 13 days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — full a la carte breakfast with all your favorites from the trip: eggs, fresh fruit, Thai pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — grilled seafood platter, fresh spring rolls, cold coconut, and tropical sorbet
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a top island restaurant — whole steamed fish with ginger and soy, Thai basil prawns, vegetable stir-fry, and a decadent Thai dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-essential items tonight to make the final morning departure smoother. Confirm checkout time and transfer logistics with the hotel. Set aside any perishable food items or opened liquids that cannot be packed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a quiet walk along the shoreline, breathe in the salt air, and say goodbye to paradise. Enjoy a final breakfast at the hotel before checkout. The hotel's butler team assists with luggage and departure arrangements.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to the ferry terminal or airport for onward travel. If time permits before departure, stop at a premium Thai supermarket or airport duty-free to stock up on Thai pantry essentials — fish sauce, curry pastes, dried herbs, premium jasmine rice, and artisan Thai teas and coffees to bring the flavors of Thailand home.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Thailand with extraordinary memories, a refined palate, and a deep appreciation for the beauty, culture, and cuisine of this remarkable destination. Safe travels.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — final breakfast: fresh tropical fruits, yogurt, pastries, eggs to order, and a farewell cup of Thai iced coffee
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or in-transit meal — opt for one last Thai dish if available, such as a bowl of Tom Yum noodle soup
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all checkout procedures, settle any outstanding bills, and leave a gratuity for the butler and housekeeping staff who made the stay exceptional. Ensure all purchased items comply with customs regulations for your home country — particularly regarding food products, plants, and antiques.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
